parts.text: Evaluate the current Gemini Supervisor program against Agents.md.

Using the current Agents.md, the current send-to-gemini.js, and your prior evaluation in this evaluator conversation, produce a complete revised version of send-to-gemini.js with every supported correction applied. Re-check the prior findings against the current Agents.md first, because Agents.md has changed since your previous evaluation. In particular, incorporate the current Step 3 executor and supervisor requirements to read evaluation-tests.md and evaluator-definitions.md at the beginning of their respective Step 3 work; implement the Step 3 internal Loop_Decision/return_to behavior; preserve the exact supervisory_gate.gate_result transition behavior and missing-key repair branch that previously passed; correct any other runtime behavior that conflicts with the current Agents.md. Do not truncate the JavaScript, omit unchanged sections, or return a patch. Return the entire replacement program. If a requirement cannot be implemented without inventing an unspecified external interface, identify it as unresolved rather than fabricating an implementation.

Using the CURRENT Agents.md and CURRENT send-to-gemini.js, produce the complete replacement send-to-gemini.js implementing the new Bootstrap procedure and preserving all previously corrected behavior. The trigger envelope contains run_nonce and nextmessage. run_nonce must be validated as a path-safe identifier and must select an isolated run container at ChatMachines/GeminiSupervisor/runs/<run_nonce>/ containing state.json, messages.json, and store/store.json. Initialize those files when the run is new. Persist the same run_nonce in current_state.run_nonce, messages.json.run_nonce, and store/store.json.run_nonce and refuse mismatched association. Preserve the verbatim trigger user message as the initial run message. Every semantic-operator input/return exchange appended to that run's messages.json must also be persisted in that run's store/store.json with the same run_nonce, including execution, JSON repair, Step 3 internal-loop/transition repair, supervisory gate, and supervisory repair calls. A new run_nonce creates a separate procedure run; reusing a run_nonce resumes that same run without reading or mutating another run. Preserve current Step 3 evaluation-document behavior, Step 3 internal transition behavior, exact supervisory_gate.gate_result PASS/FAIL behavior, and missing-key repair behavior. Use exact Step 3 transition paths from Agents.md, including nested value fields where the schema defines them. Return the entire non-truncated replacement program, not a patch.

Evaluate the CURRENT Agents.md and CURRENT send-to-gemini.js specifically for the supervisory gating defect identified by the user, then produce a revised complete replacement send-to-gemini.js that corrects the defect while preserving the rest of the current procedure behavior. The user states that the supervisory return schema should begin unevaluated, with evaluative/result fields initialized to null rather than pre-populated as PASS/FAIL or otherwise prompting the supervisor toward a result. The supervisor semantic operation should receive the execution return plus the unevaluated supervisory schema/template, perform the evaluation, fill the schema, and only then may the controller inspect the resulting exact transition key defined by Agents.md. Determine the correct implementation from the canonical Agents.md rather than merely accepting this wording mechanically. In particular, evaluate whether the current prompt construction improperly asks Gemini to manufacture a completed supervisory schema without being anchored to an unevaluated schema/template, and whether the controller is merely validating the presence of PASS/FAIL instead of enforcing the intended gate procedure. Correct all material gating discrepancies you find. Preserve Bootstrap/run_nonce isolation, per-run state/messages/store persistence, Step 3 evaluation-document requirements, Step 3 internal loop semantics, restart-on-FAIL behavior, and missing/invalid-return repair behavior unless the canonical procedure requires a change. Return the entire non-truncated replacement send-to-gemini.js source, not a patch, with no markdown fences or explanatory prose.

Evaluate the CURRENT canonical ChatMachines/GeminiSupervisor/Agents.md itself against the supervisory-gate failures observed in the most recent Gemini Supervisor runs. Treat Agents.md as the object under evaluation. Do not revise send-to-gemini.js in this run and do not substitute your own controller architecture. Determine whether Agents.md is sufficiently explicit to force the intended behavior, and identify any missing, ambiguous, or internally inconsistent requirements that allowed these failures:

1. Step 0 should fail immediately when its required execution return schema is missing, malformed, incomplete, not verbatim, has a mismatched run_nonce/request nonce, or is not persisted as required. No later step may execute after a failed Step 0 gate.
2. The supervisory gate must begin from an UNEVALUATED schema/template: every evaluative/result field starts null (including granular terminal evaluations/comments, step-level evaluation/comment, Step 3 evaluation_documents_read where applicable, and gate_result). The supervisor semantic operation must fill that template from the execution return before the controller may inspect the transition result.
3. The supervisor must evaluate the actual deliverable required by the user request. In the recent skill-generation run, the requested deliverable was the replacement bootstrap skill. The generated skill omitted required return-schema examples and still should have been rejected. Evaluate whether Agents.md explicitly requires checking the user-requested deliverable against every stated requirement rather than accepting downstream output merely because later schema fields are populated.
4. The bootstrap skill must carry enough concrete procedural context that a model can execute mechanically without inference, including explicit examples of the Step 0 execution return, an unevaluated supervisory input, completed PASS and FAIL supervisory returns, restart-on-FAIL behavior, Step 3 loop behavior, and commit/checkpoint behavior. Determine whether Agents.md requires these examples when the user asks for a detailed informational bootstrap skill, or whether a requirement must be added so omission causes FAIL.
5. A procedure with N defined steps must require at least N durable Git commits attributable to that run, with each completed step/gate boundary persisted and committed before advancing. Retries/loops may increase the count. If fewer than N commits exist for a completed N-step procedure, completion must be automatically FAIL. Evaluate whether Agents.md currently states this strongly enough; if not, identify the exact amendment needed.
6. The initial user request must remain the actual external user utterance. Internal controller prompts such as 'Perform exactly Step N' must never be incorporated into the preserved user_request/U or evaluated as if they were part of the user's request. Determine whether Agents.md sufficiently separates these contexts.
7. A successful later step must never cure or bypass an earlier failed prerequisite or gate. The first failed gate blocks progression until the same step is corrected and passes.

Use the complete current Agents.md as the authoritative source and compare each observed failure to the exact governing language. Distinguish: (a) requirements already present but violated by implementation, from (b) requirements missing or ambiguous in Agents.md itself. For every missing/ambiguous requirement, propose exact replacement/additional Agents.md text and where it belongs. Also provide concrete return-schema examples for the gate behaviors above so the specification can be executed mechanically. Do not change any repository file other than the evaluator outputs produced by this evaluation run. Return an implementation-ready evaluation with no unresolved hand-waving.
